after.description: Only messages sent at or after this instant, as an RFC 3339 timestamp such as `2026-01-31T09:00:00Z`.

before.description: Only messages sent strictly before this instant, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

Handed to the phone, which has not confirmed it went out.
The carrier took it. On an SMS thread and on most groups this is as far as it ever gets.
The recipient's device acknowledged it. An RCS and carrier feature; do not wait for it on SMS.
The recipient read it. An RCS feature, and only when they have read receipts on.
It did not go out. The message carries the reason.
An incoming message, which has no send state of its own.
null, or the argument omitted altogether: do not filter on delivery state at all.

name: remove_reaction
description: Take back a reaction the owner sent. Address it either by `reaction_id`, or by `message_id` plus `emoji`; supplying neither is `invalid_request`. Removing somebody else's reaction is refused. Repeating this call with the same client_request_id returns the same operation and sends nothing further. client_request_id.description: An idempotency key you invent for this call -- any string up to 200 bytes; a UUID is the obvious choice. Repeating this call with the same client_request_id returns the same operation and sends nothing further. A fresh client_request_id is a different call, not a repeat.

emoji.description: Which reaction to remove, as the same bare emoji that was added. A bare emoji. Google's own picker offers eleven -- 👍 😍 😂 😮 😥 😠 👎 🤔 😢 😡 ❤️ -- and anything else is sent as a custom reaction that may not render on the recipient's phone. reaction_id.description: The reaction to remove, as a `react_` ID read from the message. Supply this, or `message_id` plus `emoji`.

name: send_message
description: Send a text, an attachment, or both into an existing thread. **This sends a real SMS, MMS or RCS message to a real person. There is no sandbox and no undo.** The result carries a `message_id` and an `operation`; watch the message's `delivery.state` to learn whether it arrived, remembering that on SMS and on groups it usually stops at `sent`. Repeating this call with the same client_request_id returns the same operation and sends nothing further. A fresh client_request_id is a different call, not a repeat.

client_request_id.description: An idempotency key you invent for this call -- any string up to 200 bytes; a UUID is the obvious choice. Repeating this call with the same client_request_id returns the same operation and sends nothing further. A fresh client_request_id is a different call, not a repeat.

conversation_id.description: The thread to send into, as a `conv_` ID. It already names its own account, so there is no `account_id` here.

force_rcs.description: True to refuse to fall back to SMS: if the thread cannot carry RCS the send is refused rather than quietly downgraded.

text.description: The message body. Optional only when `upload_ids` is present, in which case it is the caption.

upload_ids.description: The attachment to send, as a one-element array of an `upl_` ID from `create_upload` whose bytes you have already uploaded. Exactly one element is accepted today; two is refused naming the limit. An upload can be sent only once.

folder.description: Move the thread to this folder: `inbox`, `archived` or `spam`. Omit it to leave the folder alone.
